findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: subscribe_event · Private data: get_market_structure, get_regime, list_history_dates, create_guest_key, get_credit_balance · Public sink: subscribe_event · Destructive: unsubscribe_event.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: subscribe_event · Private data: get_market_structure, get_regime, list_history_dates, create_guest_key, get_credit_balance · Public sink: subscribe_event · Destructive: unsubscribe_event

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

detail: Tool "list_history_dates" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.

evidence.snippet: before: "Available historical SPX market-structure replay dates." → after: "Free catalog of available historical SPX market-structure replay dates. No API key required; actual replay datasets are paid."

remediation: Re-review the tool before continuing to trust it.
